What counts as the S&P 500 value:
Only the index level calculated by S&P Dow Jones Indices, to two decimal places.
ETFs, futures, options, perpetuals, and constituent stock prices do not count.

Trading days:
Only days with an official S&P 500 close count (Eastern Time). Weekends and market holidays are ignored.
On early closes or halts (including circuit breakers), the official close designated by S&P Dow Jones Indices governs.

Index changes:
Changes to constituents, weightings, divisor, or methodology do not affect the contract.
If the index is renamed, rebranded, or re-coded but its record continues, the contract stays open. If it is discontinued with no successor, the No-data rule applies.

No data:
If no Source Agency publishes a value by the Expiration Date (including if markets are closed for the entire period), all markets resolve No, unless a "No data" strike is listed, in which case that strike resolves Yes.

Corrections:
Corrections published before Expiration govern; corrections published after Expiration are ignored.
If Kalshi finds a material error, it may delay Expiration until a corrected value is published. If none is published by the Expiration Date, the No-data rule applies.

For an 8:45am ET observation, use the 8:44am candle, covering 8:44:00am up to but excluding 8:45:00am ET. No averaging applies. The closing Pyth yield, expressed as a percentage, is rounded to five decimal places using round-half-up before comparison with the strike.

Other sources and stale or carried-forward values cannot substitute. If reliable data is unavailable by expiration, or none is expected, settlement is at the Exchange-determined last fair price, unless a "No data" strike is listed. Corrections, expiration and Rule 7.1 review follow the full contract rules. Kalshi is not affiliated, associated, authorized, endorsed by, or in any way officially connected with the Pyth Data Association. All trademarks, logos, and brand names are the property of their respective owners.

The economic event named in the title provides context. The published observation date and time govern; a delayed or rescheduled economic release does not automatically change that observation time.
